stories.headline: Nepal flash floods: SDRF on high alert in Uttarakhand's border district of Champawat
stories.deck: According to officials, apart from the SEOC numbers—0135-2710334, 2710335, 2664314, 2664315, 2664316, and 8218867005—people can also contact the toll-free number 1070
stories.bodyText:
Vigilance has been stepped up in Uttarakhand's border district of Champawat following severe floods in Nepal on Wednesday (August 26, 2026). The Tanakpur post of the SDRF has been placed on high alert, and people have been urged to stay away from the banks of the Sharda River, officials said.
According to officials, the Tanakpur post in Champawat district has been put on high alert under the instructions of State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) Commandant Arpan Yaduvanshi.
The SDRF's Tanakpur team is continuously monitoring and patrolling vulnerable riverbank areas, including the Sharda Ghat, the Sharda Barrage, and surrounding localities. The team is keeping a close watch on the river's water level and potential risks while maintaining coordination with the local administration.
Officials said that the SDRF team visited the Sharda Ghat and low-lying areas to alert local residents, travellers and fishermen about the potential rise in the river's water level. People have been urged not to venture near the riverbanks unnecessarily under any circumstances and to adhere to safety guidelines issued by the administration.
They added that the SDRF team is fully prepared round-the-clock with essential life-saving and rescue equipment to initiate immediate relief and rescue operations in the event of any emergency.
The Uttarakhand government has also issued helpline numbers to assist the state’s people stranded there.
Officials said that the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) has released these helpline numbers to aid the people.
If any person from Uttarakhand is stranded in the affected area of Nepal, or if anyone wishes to share information regarding an individual, they can contact the helpline numbers of the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Dehradun.
According to officials, apart from the SEOC numbers—0135-2710334, 2710335, 2664314, 2664315, 2664316, and 8218867005—people can also contact the toll-free number 1070.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has expressed deep grief over the extensive loss of life and property caused by the natural disaster in Nepal.
CM Dhami said that the sympathies of the people and the government of Uttarakhand are with the affected families in Nepal during this difficult time.

stories.headline: Only 20% LPG consumers applied for PNG connections
stories.deck: The transition from LPG to piped gas has seen a mere 20% uptake among eligible consumers, which remains a concern for the government despite extensive promotional efforts. Households have been targeted with informational notices and camps, but the challenge persists. To spur conversion, new incentives for distributors are being rolled out, complemented by the introduction of nodal officers to…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI:
 Only about 20% of LPG consumers who have a PNG network in their neighbourhood and can switch to the cleaner fuel have actually converted to piped gas despite govt’s push following the military conflict in West Asia earlier this year.
Of the 21.7 lakh consumers identified by city gas distribution (CGD) companies as having access to a PNG network and being eligible to switch, only 4.4 lakh have applied so far, while connections of 3.3 lakh consumers have been activated, govt data showed.
These consumers are spread across more than 72,000 housing societies in 311 geographical areas where PNG networks are available through oil companies, and public sector and private CGD entities.
Data also showed that more than 21 lakh households were sent WhatsApp messages and eight lakh were given physical notices to switch to PNG. More than 33,000 camps were also organised, but conversion remained low. In the last five months, a little over 1.4 lakh households surrendered their LPG connections.
While the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board had launched two campaigns to promote PNG, the real push came from govt during the peak of the West Asia conflict in March and April, when supplies through the Strait of Hormuz were disrupted and India faced a squeeze on LPG imports.
Of the 33 million tonne of LPG consumed in 2025-26, India domestically produced about 13 MT, while the remaining requirement was met through imports, mostly from West Asia. In comparison, India is relatively more comfortable with LNG supplies and domestic gas production.
The petroleum ministry in March issued an order to accelerate pipeline infrastructure, ease approvals and promote a shift from LPG to PNG to strengthen energy security. It also asked CGD and oil companies to communicate with LPG consumers who had a PNG network in their area, asking them to switch to piped gas within three months or risk discontinuation of their LPG cylinder supply.
Officials said a task force constituted by the ministry for enhancing PNG penetration and mapping LPG-PNG consumers met on Wednesday, with poor conversion rates being discussed. Companies were asked to expand the PNG network. A thorough de-duplication exercise will also be carried out to identify consumers who have both LPG and PNG connections.
To accelerate the adoption of piped gas, petroleum secretary Neeraj Mittal recently wrote to the chief secretaries of all states and Union Territories, asking them to provide district-level administrative support and appoint nodal officers to coordinate with gas distributors and oil marketing companies to expand the network.

stories.headline: Nepal flash flood: Massive flood sweeps through Northern Nepal
stories.deck: The Hindu’s complete coverage of the Nepal flash floods
stories.bodyText:
Catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris that have killed at least 160 people and left hundreds more missing. The exact sequence of events is still unclear, but on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) morning, torrents of water and debris crashed downstream on both sides of the border.
Surveillance video from the Chinese side showed a wall of mud and water crashing over a building as terrified people ran away. In Nepal, a surge of water hit villages and towns on the path of two rivers - Bhote Koshi and Trishuli.
The disaster was intially described as a flood on the Nepalese side, and a mudslide by Chinese authorities. While preliminary satellite analysis points to a rock-and-ice landslide as the immediate cause, experts say a thorough assessment is needed to establish the sequence of events and whether a glacial process also contributed to the flood.
Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, citing a preliminary analysis of Planet Labs satellite imagery, said in the evening that a rock-and-ice landslide along the Nepal-China border, about 20 km northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border crossing, caused a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, a tributary of Bhotekoshi, that flowed through Timure and entered the Trishuli River. Earlier, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told Parliament that preliminary information suggested an earthquake around 8.37 a.m. triggered an ice avalanche, which was followed by the flood around 8.40 a.m. “The information needed further verification,” he said.
The recurrence of extreme floods has raised concerns among experts about disaster preparedness, infrastructure planning and risk mitigation. A construction spree along rivers in Nepal’s northern regions, driven in part by the country’s push to expand hydropower as an economic booster, has remained a concern for environmentalists and climate experts.

briefs.headline: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs: “Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life...”
briefs.bodyText: "Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. Don't be trapped by dogma — which is living with the results of other people's thinking."Explanation: Jobs is telling his audience not to waste their limited time copying someone else's life. "Dogma" means rules and beliefs handed down by others, rather than things you have worked out for yourself.He said this at Stanford University’s graduation ceremony in 20025, while telling the story of his own brush with death. A year earlier, doctors had told him he had cancer and might not live long. That experience made him see how easy it is to waste time living by other people's ideas instead of your own.The line also echoes his own choices. He dropped out of Reed College after six months but continued attending classes that interested him, including a calligraphy course that he later said influenced the typography of the Macintosh. He isn't saying don't learn from others, just don't let their thinking replace your own.About the author: Steve Jobs (1955–2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor who co-founded Apple in 1976 and later led Pixar before returning to Apple as CEO in 1997. Under him, Apple launched the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad. He gave this speech to Stanford's graduating class on 12 June 2005. It remains one of the most-watched commencement speeches ever given. Jobs died in 2011 from pancreatic cancer.

briefs.headline: Peripheral inflammation may drive brain damage in rare neurological disorder, finds NIMHANS study
briefs.deck: The study demonstrated a clear association between inflammation in the peripheral immune system and neuroinflammation in patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
briefs.bodyText:
A study by researchers from NIMHANS has found that peripheral inflammation may play a significant role in triggering brain inflammation and neurodegeneration in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP), a rare neurological disorder for which there is currently no disease-modifying treatment.
The findings, recently published in Frontiers in Immunology, provide fresh insights into how the disease develops and raise the possibility of identifying blood-based biomarkers that could improve diagnosis and potentially guide future therapeutic strategies, researchers said.
Understanding PSP
PSP is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterised by loss of balance, difficulty in walking, swallowing and speaking, as well as impairment of eye movements. Because many of its early symptoms overlap with Parkinson’s disease, it is frequently misdiagnosed during the initial stages. Although previous research has suggested that abnormal immune responses contribute to neurodegenerative diseases, the mechanisms through which inflammation outside the brain influences brain pathology have remained poorly understood.
The study, led by Monojit Debnath, professor of human genetics at NIMHANS, sought to bridge this knowledge gap by investigating inflammatory pathways both within the central nervous system and in the peripheral immune system.
Multi-pronged investigation
The researchers examined three major inflammatory pathways — the NLRP3 inflammasome, NF-κB pathway, and Th17 pathway — all of which are known to regulate immune responses. Using a multi-pronged approach, the team analysed inflammatory markers in peripheral blood and cerebrospinal fluid while simultaneously employing PET-MRI imaging to assess inflammation in the brain. The combined analysis demonstrated a clear association between inflammation in the peripheral immune system and neuroinflammation in patients with PSP.
The findings add to a growing body of evidence suggesting that several neurodegenerative disorders may not originate solely within the brain but may also involve immune processes occurring elsewhere in the body.
Hope for better diagnosis
Explaining the significance of the findings, Dr. Debnath told The Hindu that the study is the first to establish a direct connection between peripheral inflammation and brain inflammation in patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. “Finding a definite and reliable biomarker in peripheral blood is the need of the hour for the accurate diagnosis of various neurodegenerative diseases, including PSP. Our study raises hope in that direction,” he said.
Dr. Debnath said the findings strengthen the hypothesis that the immune system outside the brain plays an active role in the disease process, especially in the ongoing neurodegeneration.
Ravi Yadav, professor of neurology at NIMHANS and a senior author of this study, emphasised that understanding the relationship between systemic inflammation and brain pathology could help researchers develop simpler and more accurate diagnostic tools based on blood samples. This reduces dependence on neurological investigations, which don’t have 100% diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity, Dr. Yadav said.
Disease mechanisms
The researchers said PSP is caused by degeneration of nerve cells in brain regions that control movement and cognition and is characterised by abnormal accumulation of tau protein. While rogue immune cells are believed to contribute to this process, the factors that trigger these abnormal immune responses have remained unclear. The present study suggests that inflammatory changes occurring in the peripheral immune system may influence immune activity within the brain, thereby contributing to neuronal damage and disease progression.
Further studies involving larger patient groups would be required to validate the findings and determine whether the identified inflammatory pathways could be targeted for future therapies, Dr. Debnath said.
The study adds to the growing body of research highlighting the role of systemic inflammation in neurodegenerative disorders and offers new directions for understanding, diagnosing and eventually treating Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, he added.

briefs.headline: In the 1800s red foxes came to California and a rare rail nearly vanished
briefs.bodyText:
A red fox introduced to California more than a century ago might seem far removed from the fate of a small marsh bird. Yet the two became linked in the coastal wetlands of Southern California, where the light-footed Ridgway’s rail has struggled to survive. The bird spends much of its time concealed among cordgrass and pickleweed, moving through vegetation that provides cover and nesting sites. Red foxes, meanwhile, spread beyond the places where they were originally kept after being brought to California for hunting and fur farming in the late 1800s.
At Seal Beach National Wildlife Refuge, their presence was followed by a sharp decline in the rail population. Within seven years, the refuge had just five breeding pairs. The decline added another layer of pressure to a bird already dependent on a shrinking network of coastal marshes. Listed as federally endangered in 1969, the light-footed Ridgway’s rail remains closely tied to these fragile wetlands, where changes in habitat and the arrival of non-native predators can have consequences for a population with little room for losses.
Light-footed Ridgway’s rail has faced decline in California since 1969
The light-footed Ridgway’s rail is not the sort of species most visitors to a California wetland are likely to notice. 
Its grey-brown plumage provides effective camouflage, while its body and behaviour suit a life among dense marsh plants. It occupies coastal wetlands extending from the Santa Barbara area south towards San Diego and across into Baja California, Mexico.
Its habitat has become increasingly fragmented, leaving populations separated across relatively small patches of marsh. The species was placed on the US federal endangered species list in 1969, followed by a California endangered-species listing in 1971.
According to the US Fish and Wildlife Service, numbers remain low. A federal species review estimated that California had 308 breeding pairs in 2019, compared with 656 three years earlier. Those figures are estimates of breeding pairs rather than individual birds, but they give a sense of how limited the remaining population is.
For a species with so little room to spread out, changes within a single marsh can matter.
How red foxes were introduced to California in the late 1800s
The red fox was not simply a natural newcomer to the California lowlands. Its presence there was tied to human activity during the late 19th century.
Foxes were brought into California for sport hunting and fur farming. The animals did not remain neatly within the boundaries people intended for them. Some escaped from captivity, while others were released, including animals no longer wanted by owners or fur farmers.
From there, the foxes established populations in parts of the state. They spread through agricultural and wetland landscapes, including the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, the San Francisco Bay region and, eventually, the coastal plains of Southern California.
The original reasons for introducing the animals were economic and recreational. The effects, however, extended into ecosystems where native species had evolved without the same predator pressure.
Seal Beach’s light-footed Ridgway’s rail population fell to five pairs
For the rail, the danger was particularly serious because it spends much of its life close to the ground and breeds in marsh vegetation. A predator moving through the same habitat can reach places that might otherwise provide shelter.
The history of the species at Seal Beach illustrates the scale of the problem. According to a 2020 US Fish and Wildlife Service species review, which cited a 1994 California Department of Fish and Game report, the introduction and spread of non-native red foxes was followed by a dramatic decline in the local rail population.
Within seven years, only five breeding pairs remained at the refuge.
That decline was not simply a matter of the birds becoming less common in an abstract sense. A breeding population this small has little margin for further losses. Fewer pairs mean fewer nests, fewer young and a greater vulnerability to anything else that disrupts the marsh.
The conservation challenges facing California’s coastal rail
The rail's history also shows why the effects of introduced species can be difficult to separate from the broader changes taking place around them. Coastal wetlands have been altered by development, water management, habitat fragmentation and other pressures. A predator introduced decades earlier can become another part of that altered environment.
For wildlife confined to isolated wetlands, there may be nowhere else to go when conditions deteriorate. A bird can survive only where suitable marsh remains, and even an apparently healthy patch of vegetation may not be safe if predators can reach it.
This creates a difficult conservation problem. Protecting habitat is necessary, but habitat alone does not necessarily remove the threats that have accumulated within it.
The long-term impact of California’s red fox introduction
The red fox story is more than a historical footnote because introduced populations can persist long after the original activity that created them has disappeared. The people who brought foxes to California in the 1800s could not have known how those animals would interact with a rare coastal rail generations later.
That is part of what makes introduced species such complicated conservation issues. The original decision may have been made for a short-term purpose, while the ecological consequences can continue for decades.
By the time a native species begins to decline, the chain of events behind the problem can be difficult to see. The landscape may look natural. The predator may look as though it belongs there. Yet neither necessarily has a long evolutionary relationship with the species at risk.
The uncertain future of California’s light-footed Ridgway’s rail
The light-footed Ridgway’s rail has persisted despite those pressures, but its numbers show how precarious that survival remains. Hundreds of breeding pairs may sound like a sizeable population until they are spread across fragmented coastal wetlands and exposed to changing conditions.
The bird's future therefore depends on more than its ability to reproduce. The marshes must continue to provide suitable cover, food and nesting areas, while threats from predators and other pressures need to be managed.
For a bird that spends much of its time hidden among reeds and marsh vegetation, its decline can happen largely out of public view. The history behind it is much easier to see: a species introduced for human purposes, a predator that found a new home, and a native bird left dealing with the consequences long afterwards.

briefs.headline: Former Malaysian PM Ismail Sabri charged with concealing assets
briefs.deck: The anti-graft agency in March last year said Ismail Sabri had submitted an assets declaration after being ordered to do so as part of its investigation into alleged graft and money laundering, following the seizure ‌of nearly $40 million in assets allegedly linked to him.
briefs.bodyText:
Former Malaysian Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged on Thursday (August 27, 2026) with failure to declare assets, the third former premier prosecuted in recent years over alleged graft-related offences.
Ismail Sabri, who was Malaysia’s Prime Minister for just over 15 months from 2021 to 2022 during a period of political upheaval, was accused of concealing assets that consisted of local and foreign currencies as well as gold bars and silver.
Ismail Sabri’s defence counsel, Amer Hamzah Arshad, said at a press conference that the charge was essentially a failure to comply with a notice to declare certain assets.
“We will be studying the charge and as we informed the court, we are raising certain concerns about the propriety and legality of the charge but we won’t go into detail here,” he said.
Ismail Sabri pleaded not guilty at a lower court in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday (August 27) and was released on 300,000 ringgit ($74,534) bail. If convicted, he faces jail of up to five years and a fine of up to 100,000 ringgit. The anti-graft agency in March last year said Ismail Sabri had submitted an assets declaration after being ordered to do so as part of its investigation into alleged graft and money laundering, following the seizure of nearly $40 million in assets allegedly linked to him.
Cash amounting to 170 million ringgit in various currencies and 16 kg of gold bars were seized following the raids, the agency said at the time.
A trained lawyer, Ismail Sabri has served in various roles in politics, including lawmaker and cabinet minister under three prime ministers, with portfolios that included rural and regional development, agriculture and domestic trade.

briefs.headline: Nepal floods: Aerial views show trail of destruction after massive debris surge
briefs.bodyText:
Nepal came under the sudden force of a massive flood on Wednesday, leaving a trail of devastation as the Himalayan fury claimed at least 165 lives and left more than 1300 people missing.
The Himalayan nation’s northern region bore the brunt of the disaster, with Rasuwa district on China-Nepal border among the worst-hit areas.
The fury was carried by the Bhote Koshi River, which originates in 
Tibet
 and came rushing down with enormous force, carrying with it ice, rocks, mud and debris.
The aftermath offers a stark picture of the destruction left behind. Villages appear wiped out, roads have vanished and entire stretches of civilisation seem to have been swept away by nature’s fury.
Nuwakot, barely 50 kilometres and around a two-hour drive from Rasuwa, bears the deadly imprint of the floods. The river appears to have changed course, pushing aside the settlements that once stood along its path and spreading a vast stretch of muddy debris across the landscape.
The flood tore through the Sino-Nepalese border region, destroying almost everything in its way, sweeping away vehicles, ripping apart roads and engulfing entire villages in the northern Himalayan region.
The debris that ravaged Rasuwa and surrounding areas was a deadly mix of ice, rock and mud that rushed into the Bhote Koshi River, turning it into a torrent of destruction.
The scale of the disaster also highlights a wider and growing threat facing the Hindu Kush Himalayas. Floods, landslides, avalanches and droughts are becoming more frequent and severe across the region, while rapid changes to water, land and air are posing a major threat to millions of people, according to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).
The organisation said on Wednesday that the flash flood sent a powerful surge of water, sediment and boulders through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems.
In the downstream Galchhi area, water levels in the river reportedly rose by as much as nine metres, nearly 30 feet, in just 30 minutes.

stories.headline: Restoring lakes by going beyond quick fixes
stories.deck: In cities such as Hyderabad, Bengaluru, and Mumbai, peri-urban land that once served as agricultural fields or natural lake catchments has mutated into prime real estate
stories.bodyText:
Covering nearly 6% of the planet’s surface, wetlands — including urban lakes — are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth. They store a disproportionately large share of the world’s carbon, often outperforming terrestrial forests per unit area. Beyond carbon sequestration, they contribute immensely to biodiversity, climate regulation, and human well-being. Yet today, lakes are disappearing at an alarming pace. Many of our remaining urban wetlands are either biologically dead or heavily eutrophic. In losing them, cities are systematically eroding their natural defences against climate change, undermining public health, and threatening the very foundations of urban liveability.
The widespread destruction of water bodies is a direct consequence of rapid, unplanned urbanisation. As land pressure intensifies in crowded localities, developers and municipal bodies view these natural landscapes as vacant land rather than critical ecological infrastructure. This mindset makes lakes highly vulnerable to encroachment and systemic disappearance.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s risk-averse force
briefs.deck: Police have been cautious in their approach to protests, irrespective of who is in power
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru City Police recently registered a suo motu FIR against a woman for holding a placard which read “Umar Khalid Zindabad”, “Sharjeel Imam Zindabad” at a students’ protest. Neha Bora, National President of the All India Students’ Association, during her visit to Bengaluru last week, slammed the Congress government in Karnataka for its action and said that parties who claim to be against the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) must lead by example rather than pay lip service.
This is not an isolated incident. Even as senior Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have been vocal about Israel’s war on Palestine, the Bengaluru Police booked three suo motu FIRs against pro-Palestine demonstrators. Two of these have been quashed by the High Court of Karnataka. Police even disrupted multiple indoor meetings where pro-Palestine films and issues were being discussed. While no police permission is needed for indoor meetings, the unwritten rule in Bengaluru seems to be that the local police need to be kept in the loop.
Extreme caution
Irrespective of the party in power, the Bengaluru City Police have been accused of being “risk averse” regarding protests and dissent. The police have often weaponised the Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021, which mandates that all protests can be held only at Freedom Park.
The order came in response to a suo motu PIL taken up by the High Court over protests causing traffic disruptions. Significantly, it also came close on the heels of protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, during the BJP’s tenure, when the pavement outside a mosque called Bilal Bagh turned into a site of protest. Several activists argue that protests being restricted to Freedom Park are ghettoised and invisibilised. A campaign to reverse the 2021 order, after the Congress came to power in 2023, has not yielded any results.
The police argue that they did not allow pro-Palestine protests, for if they had, right-wing groups too would have held pro-Israel demonstrations and the situation may have escalated. Recently, stand-up comic Kunal Kamra had to shift his stand-up show at a venue in Whitefield, after a little-known Hindutva outfit opposed it. To the government’s credit it ensured he performed at another venue. Earlier, shows by stand-up comic Munnawar Faruqui were cancelled twice during the BJP regime following a similar campaign.

Persistent campaigns by Hindutva groups prompting the police to either deny permission or try to make venues back out are not uncommon.
In a rare instance, recently, the police gave security for a discussion on Umar Khalid’s book at the Bangalore International Centre, after the organisers refused to back down despite a campaign. However, the police registered a suo motu FIR against a woman for holding a placard hailing Umar Khalid, following a shrill campaign by Kannada television news media.
A slow approach
Despite the Congress coming to power with a thumping majority in 2023, a rare feat in Karnataka in decades, it has been slow in countering the Hindutva agenda, for fear of what has been called “playing into the hands of the BJP.”
For instance, following the new Home Minister Priyank Kharge’s face-off with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) over it not being registered and that it should take government’s permission before using public spaces, the State Cabinet recently approved the Karnataka Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bill, 2026. However, it was not tabled in the just-concluded legislature session. Even as Mr. Kharge insisted on the RSS taking permission for their Vijaydashmi route march in his constituency Chittapur in 2025, the RSS was allowed to hold route marches in 100 places to mark its centenary.
Neither has the Congress repealed the two “communal laws” — the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020, and the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022 — it promised to roll back in its 2023 manifesto.

briefs.headline: Karnataka govt. to call special legislature session on Kasturirangan report
briefs.bodyText:
Reiterating Karnataka’s opposition to the Kasturirangan report, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Wednesday announced a special session of the legislature to discuss the consequences of implementing the report and pass a resolution in this regard.
“The Centre has notified the draft, and we have to file our objection. The draft notification has shocked us. We will call a special session, pass a resolution against it and send it to the Centre,” Mr. Shivakumar told presspersons here.
Pointing to an earlier Cabinet decision of September 2024 that rejected the report, he said: “Under the Siddaramaiah-led government, the Cabinet had rejected it. It was not considered by the Centre and it has now unilaterally notified the draft.”
In Karnataka, according to him, livelihood and farming will be affected in 1,449 villages, 33 taluks and 10 districts, which spans 20,668 square kilometres.
“We will do what is required to protect the people. Legal experts are also being consulted, and technical advice is also being sought. The draft notification imposes tough conditions on developing infrastructure, mining, power, construction, tourism and road, among others. We are also aware that there is one rule for Karnataka and another for others,” he said.
Drought to be declared
As the ground report to assess the failure of rainfall and prevailing drought conditions have been completed for 102 taluks, the Revenue Department will be declaring drought in a day or two, Mr. Shivakumar said.
“A delegation will be taken to the Centre to seek financial assistance soon after the declaration of drought,” he said, Taluks will be declared drought-hit as and when the reports are received for the rest of the taluks, he added.
The Chief Minister, who held meetings with party legislators from across the State since Tuesday, said that several issues including drought, irrigation projects, new schemes, constituency development, guarantee beneficiaries review, SIR and Prajaseve Department were discussed, and opinion from legislators was also sought.
“Prajaseve Department will be headed by an Additional Chief Secretary, and we have asked Ministers to visit taluks on the first and the third Saturdays of every month to hear complaints and redress grievances. Over the next 18 months, all 224 constituencies will be covered and it will be taken to hobli level too. Legislators have been asked to follow up at the panchayat level,” the Chief Minister said.
Mr. Shivakumar said that 50,000 sites will be distributed in every district for the poor, and government land is being identified.
Local bodies election
Elections to several urban and rural local bodies, including five corporations in Greater Bengaluru Authority region, could be held before the year-end. Referring to the Supreme Court, Mr. Shivakumar said that corporation elections are to be held before December.
“Soon after the SIR, we will be writing to the State Election Commission to hold elections in November,” he added. “Because of the delay in elections, problems have arisen in devolution of grants and receiving central assistance,” he said.
Seven lakh members for Bharat Jodo
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said that seven lakh persons have registered for membership of Bharat Jodo Sanghas online, and the membership drive will commence offline. He said that legislators have been asked to ensure at least 100 members to each sangha, which will promote sports and cultural activities.
“One government employee locally will be appointed as mentor. The activities will help in keeping youth away from drugs and wasting time. Meetings are to be held on government school premises or community halls,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru citizens flag neighbour’s vehicles as ‘abandoned’ over parking feuds
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru residents appear to have taken advantage of the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s (GBA) abandoned vehicle clearance drive with some ulterior motives.
Of the 6,000 vehicles flagged on the ASTraM app for clearance, nearly 50% were found to be false complaints, many of which were allegedly filed amid feuds between neighbours over parking spaces on the road.
Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda had announced the abandoned vehicle clearance drive as part of a citywide footpath clearance exercise being jointly undertaken with the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP). To encourage citizen participation, the BTP created a window on its ASTraM app through which residents could upload details and photographs of vehicles that had been abandoned for a long period, along with their location.
The response was overwhelming, with more than 6,000 vehicles flagged within two weeks of the announcement. However, when the BTP and Bengaluru corporations began verifying the complaints, they found that only around 3,000 were genuine, while the rest had been wrongly flagged.
In a city where many households own multiple vehicles amid a shortage of parking space, vehicles are often parked on roads for extended periods. Disputes over such parking spaces are also common. In several cases, residents angry with their neighbours over parking have uploaded photographs of vehicles that had remained parked in the same spot for a few days, alleging that they had been abandoned, according to BTP sources.
A senior traffic police officer said many families use two-wheelers to commute to work while leaving their cars parked outside their homes . “Such cars have also been flagged as abandoned,” he said.
“In some cases, people have flagged vehicles belonging to neighbours who had travelled to their hometowns after parking their vehicles on the streets,” the officer said. There have also been instances of garage owners parking customers’ vehicles on roads, which were subsequently flagged as abandoned by residents annoyed by the parking.
While no action has been taken against those who made such complaints, the police have urged citizens to flag only genuine cases, pointing out that verifying false complaints places an additional burden on personnel.
“It is a waste of time and manpower to verify such cases, which could otherwise be used to provide citizen services. Citizens should therefore refrain from making such complaints,” the officer said.
According to corporation sources, more than 1,000 vehicles have been cleared so far under the drive. These include vehicles whose owners contacted the corporation after notice stickers were pasted on them and subsequently removed the vehicles themselves after paying the prescribed fines.

briefs.headline: Over 36,000 consumers await new LPG connections in Karnataka after West Asia war
briefs.bodyText:
Following the West Asia war, the issuance of new LPG connections was temporarily halted across the country as vital import routes through the Strait of Hormuz were disrupted. Since April 2026, oil companies in Karnataka, including Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), have received around 36,069 applications for new connections.
These figures were revealed by Minister for Food and Civil Supplies Rizwan Arshad while replying to an unstarred question raised by Member of the Legislative Council Tippanna Kamaknoor in the Council recently.
Mr. Arshad said, “From April 2026 to July 2026, around 36.62 lakh LPG cylinders were delivered to consumers across the State. However, after the war involving Israel, the United States and Iran began in April 2026, new LPG connections were not provided. The department had advised gas agencies to provide 5-kg Free Trade LPG cylinders to consumers who had applied for new connections instead of issuing 14.2-kg LPG connections.”
The Minister noted that these measures were taken in accordance with instructions from the Union government and to prioritise the supply of LPG refills to existing consumers.
“Once the situation normalises, new LPG connections will be provided to consumers across the State,” Mr. Arshad said.
He also said that the State government had urged domestic LPG producers to increase production.
Elaborating on the measures taken, Mr. Arshad said, “In the initial phase of the crisis, LPG supply to the commercial and industrial sectors was regulated to meet the demand for essential cooking gas. More importantly, C3 and C4 hydrocarbon streams, which are normally used as feedstock in the petrochemical industry, were diverted on a priority basis for domestic LPG supply.
“The Essential Commodities Act, 1955, was invoked to regulate the distribution of LPG and ensure that LPG connections were made available equitably to all consumers,” he said.
To prevent household consumers from booking additional LPG cylinders, the department introduced a minimum gap of 25 days between two refills in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas, the Minister said.
He added that, to reduce dependence on LPG, the department has taken steps to create awareness about PNG connections and the use of alternative sources of energy, including electricity, for cooking.
In addition, the department has taken measures to prevent the illegal diversion of domestic LPG cylinders for commercial use, as well as the hoarding of cylinders by hotels, suppliers and others.

stories.headline: Oil prices extend losses as Hormuz reopening hopes ease supply fears
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices extended their decline on Thursday as hopes of renewed Middle East diplomacy raised expectations that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen, easing concerns over prolonged supply disruptions.
Brent crude fell 0.5 per cent to $87.43 a barrel, heading for a fourth straight session of losses, while US West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 0.5 per cent to $81.86, on track for a fifth day of declines.
The selling followed reports that Iran and Oman were working to finalise an agreement concerning the Strait of Hormuz, a critical energy route that handled oil and gas shipments equivalent to about one-fifth of global fuel consumption before the conflict began.
Qatar's prime minister is also due to travel to Iran on Thursday to revive diplomatic talks aimed at ending the nearly six-month-old conflict. The US has halted attacks on Iran for about a month, while seeking greater economic pressure on Tehran.
However, uncertainty over the waterway remains. Iran has indicated that Hormuz would not fully reopen unless the US meets its conditions under a ceasefire arrangement that later broke down. 
Analysts said the continued risk to shipping means a war premium could remain embedded in oil prices.
Supply concerns are also emerging in diesel markets. US distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, fell by 2.2 million barrels in the week to August 21, reaching their lowest seasonal level on record, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

stories.headline: Bajaj General Insurance unveils health cover for families with pets
stories.deck: The policy covers in-patient hospitalisation, room rent, road and pet ambulance services, pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses, domiciliary care, modern treatment methods.
stories.bodyText:
Bajaj General Insurance has launched ‘My Family Complete’, a health insurance plan that expands the definition of family to include pet dogs and cats.
The plan aims to address fragmented health protection by bringing human family members and pets under a single insurance policy. It offers sum insured options ranging from ₹5 lakh to ₹5 crore, with policy tenures of up to five years and a combination of indemnity- and benefit-based payouts. Dogs and cats aged three months and above are eligible, with no upper age limit.
Bajaj General Insurance MD and CEO Tapan Singhel said insurance needs to evolve with changing lifestyles and family structures. “When pets are family, their health and wellbeing naturally become a part of the family’s healthcare needs. We are responding to this need by bringing pets into the family health insurance fold,” he added.
The policy covers in-patient hospitalisation, room rent, road and pet ambulance services, pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses, domiciliary care, modern treatment methods, AYUSH hospitalisation (for humans), organ donor expenses and family visit reimbursements.
For pets, the plan includes benefits such as reimbursement for advertising and rewards when a pet goes missing, emergency pet accommodation if the pet parent is hospitalised, and third-party liability coverage for injury, death or property damage caused by the insured pet.

The JSW Group has put its proposed battery manufacturing plant in Odisha on hold as it continues to look for a technology partner for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells, Parth Jindal, Director of JSW MG Motor India and Managing Director of JSW Cement and JSW Paints, said on Wednesday.
“We are very keen to make cells in India. But the LFP technology currently is not available for us. The hunt is on for a technology tie-up. We have not yet secured a technology tie-up, and hence, that project currently is on hold,” Jindal said in Mumbai.
The company has already commissioned its cell-to-pack assembly line through JSW Energy for battery energy storage applications, as well as a cell-to-pack facility for JSW MG Motor India, he said. However, manufacturing battery cells remains a key challenge for the group, particularly because of the limited availability of LFP technology outside China.
“Making the cell, which is the key, the most important and most crucial part of an electric vehicle, that technology on LFP is not available anywhere in the world outside of China. And right now, they [the Chinese] are guarding it like a weapon,” Jindal said.
The JSW Group had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Odisha government in February 2024 to establish an integrated electric vehicle and battery manufacturing facility in the state, with a proposed investment of ₹40,000 crore.
Under the proposed project, the group was to set up a 50 GWh electric vehicle battery manufacturing plant at Naraj in Cuttack.

briefs.headline: At 18k, India sees most mobile threat detections in 8 Apac markets: Report
briefs.deck: Across the eight Apac markets studied, the average number of mobile threat detections per affected user increased 49% year-on-year to 7.3 in the first quarter, from 4.9 a year earlier. The increase came even as the overall number of users encountering threats declined, suggesting that cybercriminals are concentrating their efforts on a smaller set of targets and attacking them more repeatedly.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India recorded the highest number of mobile threat detections among eight Asia-Pacific markets analysed by cybersecurity firm Kaspersky in the first quarter of 2026, highlighting the growing risks for users as attackers become more persistent and sophisticated.
India saw 18,187 mobile threat detections during the quarter, ahead of Indonesia at 15,163, making the two countries the region’s largest markets by threat volume, according to Kaspersky.
The company said India continues to face malware such as the Rewardsteal Trojan, which disguises itself as reward or giveaway applications to steal sensitive user information.
Researchers have also seen a resurgence of the Thamera Trojan, which can hijack devices and use them to create fraudulent social media accounts at scale.
Across the eight Apac markets studied, the average number of mobile threat detections per affected user increased 49% year-on-year to 7.3 in the first quarter, from 4.9 a year earlier. The increase came even as the overall number of users encountering threats declined, suggesting that cybercriminals are concentrating their efforts on a smaller set of targets and attacking them more repeatedly.
Attackers are also increasingly using fake promotions, phishing pages, fraudulent surveys and malicious advertisements to steal credentials and personal information. 
Such links are being distributed through messaging apps, SMS, social media, fake job offers and cryptocurrency promotions.
“Across Apac, mobile threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with cybercriminals combining stealthy attack techniques, persistent malware and AI-powered deception to target consumers,” said Choon Hong Chee, head of consumer channel for Apac at Kaspersky.

briefs.headline: India emerges as highest-performing market for Nestle
briefs.deck: “Emerging markets are driving growth for Nestlé across the board and India is leading the pack,” Nestle’s global CEO Philipp Navratil said in his first visit to the country, after taking the helm in Sept last year. At present, India is among its top 10 markets, and the potential to move up is “on the horizon’”, he said.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India emerged as the highest-performing market for Nestle in first half this year (CY2026) and is on track to be among its top five markets driven by “billionaire brands, volume-led growth and right value proposition across portfolio’’.
“Emerging markets are driving growth for Nestlé across the board and India is leading the pack,” Nestle’s global CEO Philipp Navratil said in his first visit to the country, after taking the helm in Sept last year. At present, India is among its top 10 markets, and the potential to move up is “on the horizon’”, he said. In FY26, Nestle India, with household brands including Maggi, Kitkat and Nescafe, reported a revenue of about Rs 23,155 crore, showing a year-on-year growth of over 14%.
“India has been an example of RIG-led (real internal growth) case for the company, which is why we are so inspired by the market. Pricing is important, but our focus is really on driving RIG-led growth.’’ Typically, RIG-led growth is selling more products (both mass and premium), and not led by pricing. “We will continue investing to support volume-led growth to tap rising consumption, urbanisation and the expansion of the middle class.
 We will not hesitate to make the investments necessary to capture that potential.’’
India is also emerging as an export hub, with exports growing sharply and its products, capabilities and talent being taken to other markets, he added. “We look at India as a place where we can scale up business services and put AI across our processes. A lot of the work we do globally on noodles, spices and other areas is also done out of India (at the R&D centre) because the capabilities, knowledge and expertise are here.’’
Navratil has backed greater transparency in packaged food labelling, saying that the company welcomes consumers making informed and healthier choices about the products they consume. “Consumers should look at labels, compare products and consider not only price, but also what goes into them, to help them make healthier, more informed choices.’’

NEW DELHI: India’s goods exports hit the $200-billion mark during the financial year up to Aug 21 on the back of a sustained over 15% rise in shipments from the country, raising expectations within govt that this fiscal, it may breach the $500-billion level for the first time.
Latest available data estimated exports during the third week of Aug at over $25 billion, a senior official said, on the condition of anonymity. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal has set an ambitious target of goods and services exports reaching the $1-trillion mark for the first time.
Exports have been driven by petroleum products. Besides, sectors such as electronics have been booming on account of robust mobile phone exports. In addition, sectors such as engineering have powered the growth, although some of the traditional segments such as textiles have remained under pressure.
The weakening of the rupee against the US dollar is seen to have added to the tailwinds by making Indian goods more competitive against some of the shipments from rival countries.
Among the destinations, flows to China, South East Asia and countries in Africa have shown significant growth during April-July, the latest period for which official data is available.
Latest data shared by EEPC India estimated engineering shipments in July 2026 to be 18% higher at $ 12.2 billion. Among key destinations, engineering exports grew to almost all countries, barring a few including Saudi Arabia, Thailand and Turkey, EEPC said on Wednesday. Exports to Saudi Arabia have been impacted by the West Asia war.
On the import side, however, there is some pressure due to higher prices of oil and fertiliser, while gold has been putting pressure given the higher prices. In July, however, there was moderation in shipments.

briefs.headline: Sugar leaves bitter taste as retailers impose caps
briefs.deck: The closing stock for sugar season 2026 (runs from Oct to Sept) is estimated at 3.9 MMT, about 25% lower than the previous year and 40% below the five-year average of 6.5 MMT, analysts at Crisil Intelligence said in a note, prompting govt to allow import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, the first such move in a decade.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Ahead of the festival of Raksha Bandhan, when demand for sugar tends to surge in Indian kitchens, consumers are in a bind. Major online grocery platforms and offline retail chains are limiting the number of sugar packs customers can buy, to manage supplies of the household staple amid a decline in stock.
“Retailers like DMart and Reliance have capped the quantity of sugar a consumer can purchase at around two or three kgs per person. The same is being done by e-commerce companies,” said an executive with a top sugar brand on condition of anonymity. Though supplies are restricted, there is no stock-out situation as of now, the person added. DMart and Reliance Retail declined to comment.
Prices are expected to continue rising in Aug-Sept and despite the approval of imports.
The closing stock for sugar season 2026 (runs from Oct to Sept) is estimated at 3.9 MMT, about 25% lower than the previous year and 40% below the five-year average of 6.5 MMT, analysts at Crisil Intelligence said in a note, prompting govt to allow import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, the first such move in a decade.
Meagre stock has also pushed up sugar prices—earlier this week, the average all-India retail price stood at Rs 63 per kg, 29% higher than Rs 48.7 per kilo a month back. This spells trouble for both consumers and companies. While people will have to pay more for sugar, demand for which hits a peak during the festive season, firms already grappling with the war-triggered commodity inflation will have to deal with more cost pressures.
Prices are expected to continue rising in Aug-Sept and despite the approval of imports, the average price increase is estimated to be around 7% from 9% earlier, Crisil said. “The industry has to be responsible amid shortage and try to prevent hoarding,” said an executive with a quick commerce platform on condition of anonymity. A check on apps Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto on Wednesday showed that companies are restricting sale of sugar packs across brands to a maximum of 2-3 units per person.
In the case of the bigger 5 kg pack of Whole Farm Grocery sugar, Blinkit allowed only one pack to be added in the evening while 1 kg and 5 kg packs of Madhur Sugar were out of stock. Swiggy Instamart capped the purchase of sugar packs at two with several packs from Madhur and Parry’s marked as out of stock. The same was the case with Zepto. On Amazon Fresh, a search for white sugar showed no results while on the D-Mart Ready app, most of the sugar brands were listed as out of stock. Mails sent to Blinkit, Swiggy and Amazon did not elicit any response.
In a bid to prevent hoarding and support market availability, govt has imposed stock limits.

briefs.headline: India wants to review, expand 15-year-old trade pact with Japan
briefs.deck: India has been seeking a review of the agreement for several years but the Japanese side was holding out. A breakthrough of sorts was achieved last month when Prime Ministers of both countries said the two sides should discuss the pact and make it more contemporary. Bilateral trade between the two countries was pegged at $27.5 billion, with India’s exports estimated at $6 billion.
briefs.bodyText:
NAGOYA: Govt Wednesday reiterated its demand for a review of the 15-year-old Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with Japan to make it more contemporary and indicated its willingness to expand scope of the pact, which is seen to have failed in delivering gains to Indian goods and services exporters.
India has been seeking a review of the agreement for several years but the Japanese side was holding out. A breakthrough of sorts was achieved last month when Prime Ministers of both countries said the two sides should discuss the pact and make it more contemporary.
“I have also discussed it with my counterpart minister, and we are hoping to work towards further expanding the scope and providing new opportunities for this relationship to grow,” Goyal said a day after he met Japan’s minister of economy, trade and industry Akazawa Ryosei.
As the next step India and Japan have to agree to the scope of the review, amid acknowledgement that there has to be give and take in the negotiations as Tokyo is not going to give up on the concessions available to it. “We haven’t got down to work on terms of reference, but once the teams have discussed, we will be open to expanding the scope, scale and the extent of the engagement because Japan today is one of our key strategic partners,” Goyal said, adding that both sides want to strengthen the partnership and have also discussed the importance of balanced trade.
Bilateral trade between the two countries was pegged at $27.5 billion, with India’s exports estimated at $6 billion, resulting in a trade deficit of $15.5 billion. The deficit for India has widened from $11 billion in 2022-23.
Goyal also said that of the $67 billion FDI (foreign direct investment) target set by the two countries, $10 billion has flown over the last 10 months, with financial services emerging that the hottest investment bet so far.
Industry has complained of cumbersome certification and registration requirements as the main reason for Indian exports failing to gain from the trade pact. On Tuesday, Ficci president Anant Goenka had said that it was virtually impossible for pharma companies to register their products here.
Goyal said commerce department is supporting industry and exporters in registrations of their products to meet regulatory requirements. “For the pharma industry, I have also requested to start registrations all across the world...they should all look at registering all across the world, including Japan.”
The minister said he has asked different industries to submit challenges they are facing in exporting goods to Japan. “Many times these challenges are more about process and language and time, and our mission stands ready to support all sectors.”

stories.headline: Shruti seeks IOA intervention: Rider alleges EFI delay on horse-owner passes
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Indian dressage rider Shruti Vora has sought the immediate intervention of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), alleging that the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI) failed to process horse owner accreditation for the Asian Games despite receiving the required documents nearly two months before the deadline.
In a letter addressed to the IOA, a copy of which is with TOI, Shruti, a member of the Indian dressage team for the Asian Games, alleged that all required horse owner details, duly notarised, were submitted to the EFI on June 3. According to her, neither she nor fellow athletes received an acknowledgement or response from the federation despite repeated follow-ups on July 13, 17, 19 and 30.
Shruti has alleged that the EFI raised the issue with the Asian Games Organising Committee in Japan only on July 29 — nearly two months after receiving the documentation from the athletes. Further reminders were sent by athletes on August 2 and 3, she said.
The matter, according to Shruti's letter, took a more serious turn on August 14, when the Asian Games Organising Committee informed the EFI that while FEI regulations permit two horse owner accreditations or passes per horse, the names of the horse owners were required to have been submitted along with the Definite Entries.
Shruti has alleged that the delay by the EFI has consequently left horse owners at risk of being denied accreditation, despite the athletes having submitted the required information well in advance.
"This is not an unavoidable administrative issue," Shruti alleged in her communication to the IOA, describing the situation as a consequence of what she termed a "serious failure" by the federation to act on documentation submitted in time.
The dressage rider also questioned whether athletes' interests and essential administrative requirements were being handled with the seriousness expected of a national sports federation representing India at the Asian Games.
For equestrian athletes, horse owners and support personnel can play an important role during major international competitions, and Shruti argued that athletes should not be made to bear the consequences of an administrative delay when they had completed the required formalities within the stipulated time.
Shruti has now requested the IOA to intervene with the EFI and the Asian Games Organising Committee and ensure that the horse owner accreditations are processed as originally requested.
She has also sought written confirmation of the resolution, stressing that the matter is "urgent and time sensitive" with the Games approaching.
The rider said repeated attempts by athletes to resolve the matter directly with the EFI had allegedly resulted in neither timely action nor meaningful communication, prompting them to seek IOA intervention.
Shruti's letter is an allegation from the athlete's side, and the claims regarding the EFI's handling of the accreditation process have not been independently established. The EFI's response to the allegations was not included in the communication shared by Shruti.
The Asian Games 2026 are scheduled to be held in Japan, with the Indian equestrian contingent preparing for the continental multi-sport event. Shruti has urged the IOA to ensure that athletes are not prejudiced by what she alleges are administrative failures beyond their control.

stories.headline: Asian Games: Questions over selections across squads
stories.deck: In gymnastics, Pranati Nayak is the lone athlete to be cleared. There is no explanation on why other gymnasts who earned nominative, by-name quotas from the Asian Gymnastics Union (AGU) were not considered.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's Asian Games squads are facing fresh selection scrutiny with questions being raised over the criteria used in gymnastics, kurash and karate.
In gymnastics, Pranati Nayak is the lone athlete to be cleared. There is no explanation on why other gymnasts who earned nominative, by-name quotas from the Asian Gymnastics Union (AGU) were not considered.
Following the 2026 Asian Championships, Nishka Agarwal earned a nominative all-around qualification while Pranati and Protistha Samanta secured nominative qualification as vault specialists. The 2025 Asian meet adds context - Pranati won bronze while Protishta finished fourth.
The 2026 championships, held after June 20, fell outside the ministry's qualification window. But if the 2025 Asian event was used as criteria, then Protishta, too, should have made the cut.
Protishta had India's best gymnastics result at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, finishing seventh and becoming the only Indian gymnast to reach the final. Pranati competed there injured and could not make the final cut. "The question is whether the framework was applied consistently for the Asian Games. 
If yes, then on that basis, Protishta and Nishka, along with men's gymnasts Tapan Mohanty and Yogeshwar Singh, also deserved consideration," said federation sources.
Kurash raises another question. India returned from the Hangzhou Games without a medal, yet a six-member team has been cleared after an initial decision by authorities not to send one. With no performance benchmark cited, the selection remains unclear.
Karate is equally perplexing. SAI had formed a committee and initially decided not to send a team, according to sources. Yet Alisha Choudhary and Chetan Bhatt have been named. The IOA barred the Karate India Organisation (KIO) from functioning as an NSF over unauthorised selection and otherviolations.
Complaint over failure to get horse-owner accreditation: Dressage rider Shruti Vora has written to IOA president PT Usha seeking urgent intervention in securing the crucial horse-owner accreditation and blaming the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI) for oversight.

stories.headline: Anthony Andrews appointed India U17 women's assistant coach
stories.deck: Anthony Andrews also serves as head coach of East Bengal FC and will continue to hold that position too
stories.bodyText:
The All India Football Federation (AIFF) has appointed Anthony Andrews as the assistant coach of the India Under-17 women's national team, with Joakim Alexandersson continuing as the head coach.
Andrews also serves as head coach of East Bengal FC and will continue to hold that position too.
He has joined the India U17 women's team in Tashkent, where the Young Tigresses are scheduled to play two international friendly matches against Uzbekistan on Thursday and Sunday as part of their preparations for the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup China 2027 Qualifiers.
The Qualifiers will be held in Malaysia from October 5 to 11, with India set to compete in Group E alongside Malaysia, Syria and Iraq.
"Having spent a significant part of my coaching career in women’s football, working across both youth and senior levels, representing the country in this capacity is a responsibility that I take with immense pride and commitment," Andrews said.
The current Indian Women's League champion with East Bengal, Andrews is the most successful coach in the league's history, having won four titles.
He guided Gokulam Kerala FC to consecutive IWL titles in 2021-22 and 2022-23 before leading East Bengal FC to back-to-back championships in 2024-25 and 2025-26.
He is the only coach to have won multiple IWL trophies.
"Over the years, I have been fortunate to work with and develop many players who have gone on to represent India at youth and senior levels.
"Those experiences have given me valuable insights into player development, talent identification, and creating environments where young players can maximise their potential. I hope to bring that experience, along with the winning culture." Andrews has also overseen East Bengal's recent success on the continental stage.
Last Sunday (August 23, 2026), he guided the club to victory in the Preliminary Stage of the AFC Women's Champions League 2026-27 in Malaysia, making East Bengal the first Indian women's club to qualify for the group stage in consecutive seasons.
Under his stewardship, East Bengal also became the first Indian women's club to win a match in the AFC Women's Champions League group stage last season.

stories.headline: Asiad-bound TT youngsters Syndrela and Payas included in TOPS Development Scheme
stories.deck: India's 10-member Asian Games squad includes Syndrela, Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale, Yashaswini Ghorpade, Sutirtha Mukherjee, G Sathiyan, Manush Shah, Manav Thakkar, Harmeet Desai and Payas
stories.bodyText:
Asian Games-bound young table tennis players Syndrela Das and Payas Jain have been included in the Sports Ministry's flagship Target Olympic Podium Scheme's (TOPS) Development group, while senior star Manika Batra's request for funding to participate in international events next month has also been approved.
The 17-year-old Syndrela, who hails from Kolkata, bagged a silver in girls' doubles and a bronze in the girls' singles events at the Asian Youth Championships in Thailand earlier this year.
Syndrela also bagged the triple National Ranking age-group titles (U15, U17 and U19 singles) in 2023, before transitioning to the senior nationals last year.
Manika, who was omitted from the Asian Games squad for failing to meet the selection criteria of requisite domestic game time, will receive funding from the Mission Olympic Cell (MOC) for taking part in the WTT Contender tournaments in Bulgaria and Kazakhstan, scheduled for September.
Earlier this year, TOPS had decided to create a focused group of young talent between the age of 14 and 17 years, specifically for table tennis.
Syndrela had been a part of that group, which aims to build India's bench strength for the 2030 Commonwealth Games and the 2036 Olympics.
Syndrela becomes a part of the scheme alongside 21-year-old Payas and Ankur Bhattacharjee, who play men's doubles.
India's 10-member Asian Games squad includes Syndrela, Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale, Yashaswini Ghorpade, Sutirtha Mukherjee, G Sathiyan, Manush Shah, Manav Thakkar, Harmeet Desai and Payas.
